passage: After the Class 10 results, four classmates faced the same choice of stream. Akash drew a table on graph paper. Science, Commerce and Humanities each got a score for interest, marks over the past year, careers, cost and family support, and he multiplied each by how much it mattered to him, so the trade-offs stopped being a vague feeling. Farida asked herself a different question: which tasks make hours disappear, instead of which stream sounds most impressive? She noticed that she lost track of time over data puzzles and debating, which pointed to Economics more than to the Science route everyone expected. Yash put his name down for Science simply because all his friends had. It felt cosy, but it said nothing about what he was good at, and by the end of the first term Physics was a struggle. Kavya heard that some schools allow a change after Class 11 and that plenty of careers can be reached in more than one way. She relaxed, chose what fitted best now, and marked the end of the first term as her time to review.

qa.q: What did Akash draw on graph paper?
qa.a: Akash drew a table scoring Science, Commerce and Humanities.

qa.q: How does the way Farida chose differ from Yash's reason, and what came of each?
qa.a: Farida looked at which tasks made her lose track of time, and it pointed her towards Economics. Yash followed his friends into Science, and Physics became a struggle by the end of the first term.

qa.q: What was Kavya feeling once she heard a change was possible?
qa.a: She felt relieved and calmer, because the choice no longer seemed permanent.

qa.q: What could Yash do now that Physics is a struggle?
qa.a: He could talk to his teacher and family about his real interests, ask whether a change of stream is possible at his school, and keep his friendships regardless. 🙂

grounding: Classmates choose a stream by scoring options, following their interests, copying friends, and treating the choice as one that can be reviewed.
